_comment: Copy to config.json and fill in for your own category. The values below are a worked example from the recruiting/HR-software category, which is the one the post walks through. Every script reads this file — nothing is hardcoded.
_competitors: domain -> display name. The domain is what gets BLOCKED as a target (their own roundup will never add you). The name is what gets COUNTED on a third-party page.
_competitor_aliases: Extra spellings to match on a page but report under the canonical name.
_vendor_hints: Adjacent vendors that are NOT your competitors. Used only to judge whether a page is a real vendor list rather than an advice article.
_stale_vendors: Vendors in your category that shut down, got acquired, or renamed. Finding one on a live page means the article hasn't been touched in two years and the editor knows it. This is the strongest hook in the system — keep the list current.
_blocked_domains: Noise: content farms, scraper networks, and the unrelated industry that shares an acronym with yours.
_listicle_signals: Cheap keyword pre-filter, run BEFORE the LLM. Printed verbatim in the post.
_category_terms: The other half of the pre-filter. A candidate must match BOTH lists, not either.
_product_gaps: Things you do NOT ship. Named explicitly in every prompt. If your agent doesn't know what you don't do, it will invent it — persuasively.
